solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Elephant perhaps finds territory around river

indicators.note: the territory abbreviation is placed around the river, enclosing it

parts.note: TER is a standard abbreviation for territory
the Usk is a river in Wales

explanation.surface: Some wildlife observer reports an elephant marking out ground beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tusker is any animal with prominent tusks, an elephant being the classic example.

clue.text: Yanks needed for this sport

parts.note: reads as Americans being required for a game, but yanks are hard pulls on a rope, which is the whole contest

explanation.definitionFit: In this contest two teams heave on a rope, so the sport is made of nothing but yanks.

clue.text: Kids messing around ultimately ignore rule about pavement in US

indicators.note: the scrambled word kids is set around the other pieces
messing about suggests the letters of kids are jumbled
ultimately points to the final letter of ignore
about here signals that the word for rule turns back to front

parts.note: a law is a rule

explanation.surface: Children fooling about in the street pay no heed to the regulations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'messing' scrambles the children's word and splits it so it can go 'around' the rest; 'about' turns the rule word, and 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'ignore'.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the paved path beside a road the sidewalk where Britons say pavement.

clue.text: One worshipped, stood up, moving back to front

indicators.note: the final letter of the word for stood up is shifted to the start

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to stand up

explanation.surface: A worshipper got to their feet and then shuffled from the rear of the church to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros was the Greek god of love, a deity revered by worshippers.

clue.text: Dramatist organised parts outside work day

indicators.note: the rearranged word parts sits outside the work abbreviation
organised implies the letters of parts are put into a new order

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: A playwright sorts out the various roles of a production around a working day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges PARTS into ST...PAR, which goes 'outside' OP to give STOPPAR, then D.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Stoppard is a celebrated British playwright, author of Arcadia and Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead.

clue.text: He got, with Hillary, to perform a cherished ambition?

indicators.note: to perform is to act out, so the letters are made to put on a different show

explanation.surface: A climber reached a summit alongside Hillary, achieving a lifelong dream.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Tenzing and Everest; Edmund Hillary is the climber. The question mark flags that the definition is figurative.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary cup of Arthurian quests is used figuratively for any long-sought, cherished goal.

clue.text: Current breaks through seaside building

indicators.note: breaks through implies one piece bursts into the other

parts.note: per means by way of, or through
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A flow of water bursts through a structure on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier is a structure built out into the sea at a resort, often with amusements.

clue.text: Fish topped with date and nut

indicators.note: topped means its head is cut off, removing the first letter

parts.note: salmon is a fish

explanation.surface: A fish dish is garnished with a date and a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is an edible nut, the seed of a tree related to the peach.

clue.text: Revolutionary politician linked with road and housing problem?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned around, so the whole string reads backwards

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A radical politician involved in road building also has a housing crisis to face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' turns both pieces, TORY and RD, reading DRYROT. The question mark: the problem is in the houses' timber, not housing policy.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay of timber that can wreck a house's structure.

clue.text: Child's dummy held in case of distress? On the contrary

indicators.note: held in signals one piece sitting inside another
on the contrary reverses the stated roles, so the case goes inside the dummy instead

parts.note: a goon is a fool or dummy

indicators.note: case of means the outer letters of distress

explanation.surface: A baby's pacifier is kept in a bag in case it gets upset.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally, the dummy would sit inside the outer letters of 'distress'; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so those letters go inside the dummy.
explanation.definitionFit: A godson is a boy for whom one stands as sponsor at baptism, a kind of child.

clue.text: Cricketer gets reward trapping Essex opener before interval

indicators.note: trapping means the reward word encloses what follows

parts.note: pay is a reward for work

indicators.note: before places the Essex letter ahead of the interval
opener means the first letter of Essex

parts.note: a term is an interval of time

explanation.surface: A batsman earns a bonus after catching out an Essex opening bat just before the break.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter May captained England at cricket in the 1950s; Essex is an English county side.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter May was a leading England batsman and Test captain of the 1950s.

clue.text: Alf and Paul, cavorting on rock, play a trick

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means the first part is placed above the next
cavorting means prancing about, so the letters of the two names jump around

parts.note: stone is rock

explanation.surface: Two friends prance about on a boulder while playing a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull a fast one is an idiom for deceiving someone with a trick.

clue.text: Loud hooter for game?

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
an owl is a hooter

explanation.surface: A noisy horn is wanted for a sporting event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hooter' suggests a car horn or a nose, but here it is the bird that hoots.
explanation.definitionFit: Game birds such as pheasant and grouse are wild fowl hunted for food.

clue.text: Unionist goes through newspaper on mattress

indicators.note: goes through means one piece penetrates the other

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, a newspaper

explanation.surface: A Unionist politician reads the paper while lying on a mattress.
explanation.definitionFit: A futon is a Japanese-style padded mattress laid on the floor or a frame.

clue.text: Release single in Italy (500 packaged)

indicators.note: packaged means wrapped inside, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: uno is Italian for one
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A single car is launched in Italy, a Fiat 500 in its packaging.
explanation.walkthrough: The 500 suggests the Fiat car, but it is just the Roman numeral D.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or fastening is to release it.

clue.text: Party friend ignores a toy

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: ignores means the letter is left out

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend at a party overlooks a toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolly is a child's word for a doll, a toy.

clue.text: Track down old pair of actors in pub

indicators.note: in means the middle pieces go inside the pub

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: pair of means the first two letters of actors

explanation.surface: Someone tracks down a pair of veteran actors in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To poach is to hunt game illegally, chasing down quarry on another's land.

clue.text: Top amateur in Floral Arrangement suggests anyone can win

indicators.note: in places these pieces inside the rearranged letters
arrangement means the letters of floral are set out anew

parts.note: lay means non-professional, amateur

explanation.surface: A leading hobbyist entering a flower-arranging contest thinks the prize is open to anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals on 'Floral Arrangement' make it look like a contest category; 'Arrangement' is the anagram signal, and its scrambled letters split to hold the top amateur.
explanation.definitionFit: When everything is still to play for, the result is undecided and either side may triumph.

clue.text: Unbalanced circles representing the flag

indicators.note: circles means the first word surrounds the others

parts.note: unbalanced means mad
as means in the role of, representing

explanation.surface: Unstable rings stand for a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's masthead, the title across its front page, is called its flag in the trade.

clue.text: Extra poster on shelter sounded foolish

indicators.note: in a down answer, on puts the poster above the shelter

parts.note: an ad is a poster
a den is a shelter

indicators.note: sounded means the word for foolish as spoken, its silent B lost

parts.note: dumb means foolish

explanation.surface: An extra advert was pasted on a hut that looked silly.
explanation.definitionFit: An addendum is an extra item added to a book or document.

clue.text: Face of rock and roll originally, in command and tough?

definitions.text: Face of rock and roll originally, in command and tough?

parts.note: a cliff is a rock face

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of roll

parts.note: IC means in charge, in command
hard means tough

explanation.surface: The front man of rock and roll was always in charge and hard as nails.
explanation.walkthrough: Cliff Richard is a British pop star who began as a rock and roller in the late 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliff Richard was Britain's first big rock and roll star, a long-time public face of the genre.

clue.text: Dramatist from US avoids playing Schubert

indicators.note: avoids means two letters of the composer's name are left out
playing suggests the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A playwright from America shuns performing Schubert.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertolt Brecht was a German playwright, author of Mother Courage.

clue.text: Below stairs, he's found only large ruler

parts.note: but means only, as in but a child
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a queen

explanation.surface: In the servants' quarters lives a man who is just a big monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below stairs' is the British term for the servants' quarters of a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: The butler is the head male servant who works in the servants' quarters of a big house.

clue.text: Rowdy mob that makes Bert bet?

parts.note: taking the letter ... of the name Bert leaves bet, so the clue is an ... instruction

explanation.surface: A mob causes a man named Bert to gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: An instruction that removes the letter R from 'Bert'; read as two words that instruction describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In old usage a rout is a disorderly crowd or rabble.

clue.text: Glaze over Salvation Army photograph

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the two letters read the other way

parts.note: pic is short for picture, a photograph

explanation.surface: A glossy finish is applied over a Salvation Army photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspic is a savoury jelly used to glaze cold meats.

clue.text: Child off chesty, shivering — it's an infection

indicators.note: shivering suggests trembling letters that move about
off means the letters for child are taken away

explanation.surface: A child with a bad chest trembles from an infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes CH from CHESTY, leaving ESTY, which 'shivering' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is a small bacterial infection forming a red bump on the eyelid.

clue.text: After depression, love such a pudding?

indicators.note: after means the love letter comes after the depression

parts.note: a sag is a depression or dip
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: After feeling low, someone craves comfort food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sago pudding is a milk pudding made from palm starch, a nursery classic.

clue.text: Britain — the greatest island?

parts.note: Muhammad Ali called himself the greatest

explanation.surface: Britain is asked whether it is the finest island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island famous as a holiday destination.

clue.text: Drink affected vocals stifling commercial

indicators.note: stifling means the rearranged letters smother the commercial inside them
affected means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ad is a commercial

explanation.surface: A drink has affected a singer's voice, muffling the jingle.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvados is an apple brandy from Normandy.

clue.text: Inferior remnant's the latest in fashion

definitions.meaning: the worthless last part left of something
taken whimsically as the end of a fag, a cigarette once highly fashionable

explanation.definitionFit: A fag end is the stub of a cigarette, and figuratively the last, poorest part of anything.

clue.text: Pastry company wants to make it big

definitions.meaning: a folded pastry case with a fruit filling

definitions.text: company wants to make it big
definitions.meaning: a firm hopes for large total sales revenue

explanation.definitionFit: An apple turnover is a pastry; a company's turnover is its total sales.

clue.text: Caribbean music fans reflected discernment

parts.note: WI is the West Indies, the Caribbean

indicators.note: reflected means seen in a mirror, so read backwards

parts.note: mods were 1960s fans of soul and ska music

explanation.surface: Caribbean music lovers looked back with good judgement.
explanation.definitionFit: Wisdom is the quality of good judgement and insight.
